title: Ancient Trees in Switzerland: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Geneva has recorded one chestnut's first spring leaf every year since 1818. The tree currently doing the job is about eleven. 6 places, 31 trees.
intro: Geneva has recorded the date a chestnut tree opens its first leaf every spring since 1818, one of the longest continuous records of its kind anywhere, and the tree currently doing the job is about eleven years old. The sautier of the cantonal parliament walks to the designated tree, checks it, and reports the date to the press. Age here tends to arrive with that sort of paperwork: five planes in the botanical garden were already mature enough to appear on a cantonal map in 1728, and the cedars of Parc Beaulieu, around 290 years old, grew from seed a French naturalist carried out of an English garden. Zurich adds four more, and Robenhausen contributes a single oak on the shore where a 19th-century dig gave a whole period of European prehistory its name. Twenty-six trees, three cities.
